Queen's College, London
first for Girls
Discover Queen's
Discover our Preparatory School for girls aged 3–11 and our College for girls aged 11–18, each offering an outstanding education in the heart of London.
Why Queen's
Queen’s College, London and Queen’s College Preparatory School offer an education shaped by nearly two centuries of pioneering spirit and a clear vision: to empower girls to lead with confidence, compassion and intellectual ambition. Since 1848, Queen’s has been at the forefront of girls’ education, challenging convention and opening doors that continue to shape futures today.
We are proudly pastorally-led, placing wellbeing at the heart of school life, because lasting success is grounded in care and belonging. Alongside this, our academic standards are ambitious and rigorous, inspiring pupils to think independently and enjoy being challenged.
Located in Marylebone in central London, our pupils draw daily inspiration from the city’s parks, museums and cultural institutions as an extension of the classroom. This powerful combination of heritage, pastoral strength and academic excellence makes Queen’s a distinctive choice.
A Welcome fromThe Principal
We live in a fast-moving age where young women have many conflicting pressures on them, and an unprecedented degree of choice as to which path they can take through life. These extraordinary times require an extraordinary school, and we believe we have one at Queen’s.
Ours is a community where success comes not from pressure, but from tolerance, kindness and respect. Supported by outstanding teaching and pastoral care, pupils learn not just their subjects, but to value themselves and each other, leaving with a clear sense of who they are and how they can make a difference.
Our academic results speak for themselves, but our pupils are our finest ambassadors.
Do come and meet them to find out more about what makes Queen’s so special.Richard TillettPrincipal

A transformative environment...
"Joining Queen’s transformed my daughter’s happiness and confidence... she now leaves for school each day with a huge smile, full of excitement. As a parent, I feel a deep sense of peace and tranquillity knowing she is so well cared for, within a warm and supportive sisterhood."
A joy-filled start...
"Nursery is a gently academic yet joy-filled start."
Outstanding results...
"No surprise students head to top universities."
- Tatler Schools Guide
Exceptional opportunities...

Well-rounded girls...

- Good Schools Guide
A culture of care...

Welcome to Queen's College Preparatory School
from our Co‑Heads Georgia Habanananda and Ailsa Buddle At Queen’s College Prep School, we believe that every child flourishes when she is known, nurtured and encouraged to be boldly curious. Our school, nestled in the heart of Portland Place in central London, is a joyful community where girls feel confident to explore.With a long and proud heritage, and the added benefit of being linked to Queen’s College, London, one of Spear's top 100 independent schools in the world, we equip girls with the knowledge, character and curiosity they need to thrive - wherever their senior school ambitions may lead them. Our commitment to exceptional pastoral care comes from our knowledge that when a child feels happy, safe and supported, she can achieve anything.
QCPS is proud to be a member of the Girls' Schools Association (GSA) and Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS). As Co‑Heads of the Prep School, we are delighted to welcome you.
A message from Georgia Habanananda
Originally from Sydney, Australia, I began my career after completing a Bachelor of Arts/Education before moving to London. I have since taught across a range of communities, including Islington, Tower Hamlets and Hackney, and across all prep year groups from EYFS to Form VI. Each stage brings something unique, and I value the different strengths and personalities that children develop as they grow. These experiences have shaped my commitment to inclusive, engaging and multi-sensory learning that enables every child to feel confident and succeed. Most recently, I completed a Postgraduate Certificate in Specific Learning Differences (SpLD) Dyslexia, a master’s level qualification. This specialist training allows me to support pupils with dyslexia and other learning differences through careful assessment and tailored teaching, helping each child to build confidence, independence and a genuine sense of achievement. My years as Head of Inclusion and Deputy Head at QCPS, where I supported children with additional needs, guiding families, and leading on safeguarding and emotional wellbeing, have shaped my belief that pastoral care is the essence of a truly great school. At Queen’s College Prep School, it is a privilege to work alongside families to ensure each girl feels seen, supported and empowered to excel. Since joining QCPS as Head of Learning Support in 2019, I have relished the opportunity to champion pupils’ strengths and celebrate the wonderful diversity of talents in our community. Outside of school, I enjoy long weekend walks, practising French, keeping fit and spending time with friends. My two children, now 16 and 13, and my partner keep life busy and full.
A message from Ailsa Buddle
My path to education began at the University of Birmingham, where I completed a joint honours degree in Hispanic Studies and Drama, followed by a PGCE specialising in Spanish at Nottingham Trent University. Over my years teaching in schools all around Nottingham and then London, I have had the privilege of working across all year groups, with particular focus on preparing pupils for key exam years and the exciting transition to senior school.Before joining Queen’s College Prep School in 2014, I was Head of Modern Foreign Languages. During my time at QCPS I have been Head of English then Head of Prep before becoming Deputy Head Academic in 2021. Throughout my career, I have been driven by the belief that every child deserves to feel confident in their abilities and inspired in their learning. Academic excellence isn’t simply about results but is about developing independent, determined thinkers who embrace challenge and are ready for whatever future they choose. Fluent in Spanish (with a little Portuguese and French too), and a lifelong lover of literature, film, and theatre, I’m passionate about fostering creativity, curiosity and global awareness in the classroom. Outside of school, you’ll find me exploring nature - on coastal paths, hill walks, or in our wonderful London parks - with my two and half year old son and seven year old daughter, or happily immersed in a good book whenever I get the chance!
Queen's College Preparatory School Values
QCPS provides an outstanding, real-world education for girls, that equips them to live with assurance and ambition. Our values are collaboration, creativity, courage, compassion and curiosity. We champion them and are guided by them every day.
Collaboration
Our pupils work and play effectively and happily in a team, respecting and valuing the contributions of their peers. They can influence, compromise, lead and work together to achieve a goal. They celebrate the achievements of others and understand the power of a common purpose.
Creativity
Queen’s pupils are creative thinkers, able to solve problems with a flexible and original approach. They are engaging speakers and writers with a talent for invention and playfulness in all that they do.
Courage
Pupils at Queen’s are prepared to get out of their comfort zone to push boundaries and ensure their personal progress. They are resilient in their approach to all that they do, confident that mistakes prove that they are learning and growing.
Compassion
Our pupils are kind to one another, polite to their elders and care deeply about global issues. They are committed to using their skills and knowledge to improve the world and help others less fortunate than themselves.
Curiosity
Committed to learning for the joy of learning, our pupils have an unquenchable thirst for knowledge. They actively and independently pursue their interests and understanding of the world to find out answers to their own ‘how and why’ questions.
Our Vision as Co-Heads
Together, we are committed to:
Championing the whole child: her wellbeing, her passions, her potential.
Cultivating curiosity that drives deep learning.
Fostering a warm, inclusive community where every girl feels known and valued.
Preparing pupils for the next steps with confidence, whether they continue to Queen’s College, London or venture to a different senior school.
Ensuring QCPS remains a place of joy, ambition and opportunity.
Queen’s College Prep School is a remarkable place and we are thrilled to lead it together. We look forward to welcoming you and your family to our community.
Georgia Habanananda and Ailsa Buddle
Co‑Heads of Queen’s College Preparatory School
Where Next?

Welcome to Queen's College, London
from Richard Tillett, Principal
Queen’s has been at the forefront of education for over 175 years. Established in 1848, Queen’s was the first British educational establishment to give academic qualifications to women. We are now one of the most high-achieving, diverse and forward-looking girls’ schools in London.
We live in a fast-moving age where young women have many conflicting pressures on them, and an unprecedented degree of choice as to which path they can take through life. These extraordinary times require an extraordinary school, and we believe we have one at Queen’s. Ours is a community where success comes not from pressure, but from tolerance, kindness and respect. Supported by outstanding teaching and pastoral care, pupils learn not just their subjects, but to value themselves and each other, leaving with a clear sense of who they are and how they can make a difference. Queen's is a community where every individual thrives.
Our academic results speak for themselves, but our pupils are our finest ambassadors.
Do come and meet them to find out more about what makes Queen’s so special.
Where Next?

Partnerships and Outreach
At Queen's College London and Queen's College Preparatory School, we know that education brings huge benefits when it extends beyond the classroom. Through partnerships with schools, charities, community organisations and local businesses, we encourage every pupil to develop compassion, leadership and a strong sense of social responsibility. From the earliest years in our Pre-School through to Senior College (Sixth Form), our pupils are inspired to make a positive difference within their local community and beyond.
Charity Fundraising and Volunteering
Supporting others is an integral part of life at Queen's. Throughout the year, pupils across both the Prep School and College take part in a wide range of charitable fundraising initiatives, developing teamwork, creativity and a commitment to helping others.
House fundraising activities are led by pupils and include everything from bake sales and creative competitions to sponsored challenges and community events. Each House supports its chosen charity, while our Sixth Form students and both Parents' Associations also select charities to benefit from their extensive annual fundraising efforts.
Community service is an important part of Sixth Form life. Every Wednesday afternoon, Sixth Form students volunteer with local schools and charities, contributing their time, skills and enthusiasm while gaining valuable experience and developing a deeper understanding of the communities around them.
Supporting Local Schools
We are proud to enjoy long-standing partnerships with local state schools, creating opportunities for collaboration, shared learning and enrichment for pupils of all ages.
Our relationship with St Vincent's Primary School is one example of this commitment. Several Queen's Sixth Form students volunteer regularly at the school, while St Vincent's pupils visit Queen's throughout the year to enjoy subject masterclasses, participate in our Primary Maths Challenge and make use of our specialist facilities. These partnerships provide enriching experiences for pupils from both schools while strengthening links within our local community.
Southwark Schools Learning Partnership
Queen's is a proud member of the Southwark Schools Learning Partnership (SSLP), a collaboration of 16 state and independent schools committed to providing exceptional educational opportunities for pupils and professional development for teachers.
Through the SSLP, Queen's regularly hosts events for pupils and staff from partner schools, including our popular Stockmarket Challenge, alongside workshops, enrichment activities and the inspiring Thinking About lecture series featuring expert speakers from a wide range of disciplines.
Find out more about the Southwark Schools Learning Partnership at www.sslp.education.
Girls Human Rights Hub
We are honoured to work closely with the Girls Human Rights Hub, founded by Sultana Tafadar KC and her daughter, a current Queen's pupil. The Hub champions the rights of girls around the world through education, advocacy and public engagement.
This partnership reflects our shared belief that girls' education should empower young women not only with academic knowledge but also with the confidence, empathy and leadership skills to make a meaningful contribution to society. Through workshops, events and collaboration with the Hub, pupils gain valuable insight into how legal expertise, advocacy and principled leadership can create lasting social change.
Queen's is proud to have signed the Hub's Global Pledge, publicly affirming our commitment to advancing girls' rights and joining an international community working towards greater equality, opportunity and justice.
Working Together
We are always keen to develop new partnerships with charities, schools, universities, businesses and community organisations that share our commitment to education, opportunity and service.
If you would like to discuss a potential partnership or community outreach project with us, we would be delighted to hear from you. Please email marketing@qcl.org.uk with details.
Where Next?

Visit Queen's
Join us at an Open Event or arrange a private visit
The best way to experience life at Queen's is to visit us in person. Whether you're exploring Little Corgis Pre-School, Queen's College Preparatory School or Queen's College, London, our Open Events and personalised tours offer the opportunity to see our schools in action, meet our staff and students, and explore our exceptional facilities.You'll have the chance to step inside classrooms, discover our broad curriculum and co-curricular opportunities, and learn more about the supportive and ambitious community that makes Queen's such a special place to learn and grow. Most importantly, you'll have plenty of opportunities to ask questions and find out whether Queen's is the right fit for your daughter.
To arrange a private tour, please contact our Admissions Team:
We look forward to welcoming you and your family.
Where Next?

Curriculum
An exceptional and well-rounded education for every pupil
Our curriculum is very broad, designed to promote excellence and to give the girls as many opportunities as possible to identify their strengths and expand their horizons. Our teachers create an inspiring and nurturing environment in which every girl is challenged and supported to reach her full potential in all areas of school life.
Exceptional specialist teaching, first-class facilities and high-quality pastoral care combine to ensure the girls grow into confident, accomplished, creative young people with emotional intelligence and high personal standards.
Explore our Subjects
Queen's College Preparatory School provides an exceptional, rounded education which harnesses the very best of traditional values with a thoroughly modern approach to education.
Our curriculum combines core subjects with the humanities to give knowledge, understanding and a sense of perspective. Our science teaching extends across technology, creativity, research and exploration, building real skills for real life; at Prep School, Senior School and beyond.
We understand that our job is to prepare your daughter for the future, not just to get her through the present. Our focus is on the development of character, motivation and self-confidence to provide skills and attitudes that will adapt as the world continues to change. Our girls are encouraged to think for themselves, to be ambitious, to be resilient and to be resourceful.
The Visual Arts curriculum is considered a vital aspect of our girls’ development at QCPS. Much of the practical work created is linked to other areas of the curriculum, enriching the pupil’s experience in art lessons while they gain a deeper understanding of history, religion, culture and science.
Art
Syllabus
Over the course of the academic year, pupils explore a wide range of processes and techniques whilst working in a variety of materials.
During lessons they explore the artwork of different artists and craftsmen in art history and which is directly linked to their practical work. This allows pupils to gain a more in-depth understanding of how artists created work to express and represent the history of their time.
The importance of self-expression and risk-taking, in a safe and supportive environment, while exercising the imagination and creativity of each individual is at the heart of our lessons.
Workshops & Educational Visits
We regularly invite 'Artists in Residence' to establish workshops in the QCPS art studio. Visiting artists offer possibilities for creative work that extend beyond the normal range.
The girls also regularly visit galleries for inspiration and to further embed their learning. Most recently, we have visited the Tate Modern, National Gallery, Tate Britain and the Victoria and Albert Museum.
Every year our school community join together to celebrate the artwork of our pupils at our annual Art Exhibition, this is representational of the large and important role that Art plays in our school.
At QCPS, we want to excite and engage our girls to be creative and confident with technology in an ever-changing and increasingly connected world.
We equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding to become responsible and digitally literate citizens, while developing their creativity, problem-solving and computational thinking.
Computer Science
Syllabus
Our Computer Science curriculum develops progressively from the Early Years onwards, with online safety embedded throughout. All girls sign an Internet Safety Agreement each academic year, with additional activities taking place around Safer Internet Day in February.
Coding begins in Reception with Bee-Bots, where girls learn the fundamentals of sequencing, giving instructions and creating simple algorithms. They then progress to block-based coding using ScratchJr and Scratch, developing their understanding of:
Alongside coding on screen, pupils use robotics to put their skills into practice, developing problem-solving, logical reasoning and debugging through hands-on challenges.
As girls move through the school, they are introduced to Python, giving them their first experience of text-based programming and building on the computational thinking skills developed in earlier years.
Pupils also develop a broad range of digital skills across the curriculum, including:
Together, these experiences help girls become confident and capable users of technology, with the skills to create as well as consume digital content.
Dance is an integral part of the weekly timetable at QCPS, giving pupils the opportunity to develop confidence and physical expression.
Through Dance, pupils explore movement, choreography and performance in an inclusive and supportive environment. Lessons encourage them to work both independently and collaboratively, developing an understanding of how movement can be used to communicate ideas and emotions.
Dance also provides an important creative dimension to the curriculum. Pupils are encouraged to take creative risks and develop their own ideas, while building confidence in performing and responding to the work of others.
Language is the key building block of culture and social interaction. At QCPS, we aim to ignite a love for English language and literature by promoting an exciting and effective curriculum, equipping our pupils with the essential language skills they need to communicate successfully and creatively.
We encourage a lifelong passion for reading in all the girls at QCPS and instil in them an ability to engage with, question and challenge any text that they encounter.

We have a creative, theme-based curriculum in Reception and Form I, where cross-curricular links are made at every opportunity.
From Form II to VI, the curriculum ensures the pupils access a variety of text types and have the opportunity to write in many different styles. From narrative to newspapers, discursive to descriptive, all pupils will master a range of skills within these genres.
Amongst many other skills, the girls will learn:
These skills will prepare them to be confident and competent readers, writers, speakers and listeners in years to come.

Workshops & Educational Visits
The department seeks to employ a full range of learning styles, catering for all educational needs. Drama workshops which cross over into history, trips to the theatre, author visits and Public Speaking Week are just some of the many ways in which QCPS seeks to enrich the curriculum and inspire our pupils.
Geography at QCPS is an opportunity for our pupils to explore our planet.
Our lessons inspire a wonder of the natural environment such as:
Our aim is to ensure we support the girls to become confident collecting, analysing and interacting with a range of data gathered through their experiences. They also learn to use an atlas, follow directions and other basic mapping skills.
Geography
Mountains
Volcanoes
The effect of weather and climate
Workshops & Educational Visits
We take advantage of our local area and embrace the vast opportunities available on our doorstep. Geography field trip activities include trips to local farms, orienteering excursions, boat trips on the River Thames and a variety of excellent workshops and exhibitions provided by The Natural History Museum.
From cultural awareness to diving headfirst into new and exciting experiences, Geography can work wonders on the minds of young children. It’s a scholastic way to broaden their minds through complete immersion!
At QCPS, History is integral to our curriculum, providing context to our contemporary global topics. Our teaching approach generates an enthusiastic and enduring interest in the subject. It allows our pupils to develop skills of enquiry and analysis, helping them to think for themselves and arrive at logical and reasoned judgements.
History fires the curiosity of our pupils, helping to cultivate an interest of the past.
During lessons, the girls consider how the past, and its relevance to the present, impact on the world today.
Pre-Prep Syllabus
In the Pre-Prep, the pupils enjoy learning about how London has changed over time, studying topics from the Great Fire of London to Florence Nightingale.
Prep Syllabus
In the Prep department, the girls explore a range of cultural histories, such as:
We teach the girls to consider alternative viewpoints, encouraging them to consider how a range of people would have reacted and reflected on the events they experienced.
The Egyptians
First and Second World War
Workshops & Educational Visits
QCPS employs varied teaching techniques including traditional historical enquiry, role-play and visits to places of historical interest and discussion.
Educational visits by all classes take place regularly to a wide variety of historical buildings and sites, and of course, museums – The British Museum being a particularly popular destination. Classes also visit venues such as Shakespeare’s Globe, The Museum of London and the Tower of London, as well as travelling further afield to visit places such as Bletchley Park, Hampton Court and The Ragged School.
Languages at QCPS are taught throughout all year groups by specialist and native-speaking teachers.
Languages
Pre-Prep Syllabus
In the Early Years at QCPS, our languages teaching focuses on sounds and gradually evolves towards reading and writing. With time, the girls retain vocabulary and gain confidence in making their own statements. They enjoy being able to communicate purposefully. The first time they realise they are able to do so is always very exciting!
At this stage the girls’ learning focuses primarily on sounds through listening and singing.
Pupils understand and communicate ideas, facts and feelings in speech and writing, focused on familiar and routine matters, using their knowledge of phonology, grammatical structures and vocabulary. At this stage the girls’ learning focuses primarily on sounds through listening and singing.
Prep Syllabus
As pupils’ knowledge of grammar improves, so does their communication and autonomy. In the Prep, they are able to extend their conversations to write and talk about themselves, their home, family and their school life.
Pupils are also exposed to French culture through a residential visit to France in Form VI, workshops, films, stories, songs and rhymes.
Years 4, 5 and 6 have a recorded assessment at least four times a year.
Form 6 exchange letters with l’Ecole Catherine Dior in Normandy and have the opportunity to spend a fun day with the children they have been writing to during the residential trip.
At QCPS we aim to develop a sense of enjoyment, confidence and competence with numbers and measures through structured teaching and learning experiences.
We follow the renowned Mathematics scheme, ‘Maths, No Problem’. This approach to teaching ensures children develop a deep understanding of topics using concrete materials and a focus on making Mathematics practical. We are determined to foster and nurture a love of numbers.
At QCPS our Mathematics mantra is simply - Maths is fun! We are proud of our excellent attainment, but high achievement in Mathematics is about more than completing assessments and results. We are determined to foster and nurture a love of numbers, a high level of confidence in, and enjoyment of, Mathematics in all aspects of everyday life.
Mathematics
Advanced Learners and Additional Support
Stretching and challenging our girls is at the heart of our lessons and we always provide plenty of opportunity for differentiation. Advanced learners are now no longer accelerated through new content but are challenged with rich and sophisticated problems within the topic being studied, stretching their understanding even further. Those children who are not sufficiently fluent are provided with additional support to consolidate their understanding before moving on.
At QCPS we firmly believe that music enriches our lives and we strive, above all, to foster a love and appreciation for music in every pupil. As Plato said, “I would teach children music, physics and philosophy; but most importantly music, for the patterns in music and all the arts are the keys to learning.”
All pupils, from Reception to Form VI, receive specialist music teaching covering the main
A creative curriculum approach links music with other subjects, making learning more relevant, immersive and fun. We believe all girls should receive instrumental tuition; therefore, we include lessons on various instruments, from whole-class ocarina, recorder and ukulele lessons, to African drumming and Indonesian gamelan music.
Music
Listening
Appraising
Composing
Performing
Music Facilities
The music department includes five bespoke music-teaching rooms, a large music classroom and the Hall, with its handcrafted S4 Yamaha grand piano. Girls have access to a host of classroom percussion instruments, as well as class sets of ukuleles, djembe and dun-dun drums, marimbas, plus online music software to aid independent home learning.
Workshops & Concerts
Pupils perform regularly throughout the year, both at large whole-school events and at smaller, informal class concerts. We attend concerts around London and take part in various music workshops in and outside of school.
At QCPS, the girls lead healthy active lives, with a rich and varied physical education programme that gives everyone the chance to develop competence and confidence.
We offer a very broad range of individual and team sports, including both indoor and outdoor activities. The PE curriculum allows all abilities to succeed in sport.

Syllabus
Over the course of the academic year, pupils explore a wide range of processes and techniques whilst working in a variety of materials.
During lessons they explore the artwork of different artists and craftsmen in art history and which is directly linked to their practical work. This allows pupils to gain a more in-depth understanding of how artists created work to express and represent the history of their time.
The importance of self-expression and risk-taking, in a safe and supportive environment, while exercising the imagination and creativity of each individual is at the heart of our lessons.
Workshops & Educational Visits
We regularly invite 'Artists in Residence' to establish workshops in the QCPS art studio. Visiting artists offer possibilities for creative work that extend beyond the normal range.
The girls also regularly visit galleries for inspiration and to further embed their learning. Most recently, we have visited the Tate Modern, National Gallery, Tate Britain and the Victoria and Albert Museum.
Every year our school community join together to celebrate the artwork of our pupils at our annual Art Exhibition, this is representational of the large and important role that Art plays in our school.
At QCPS, we want to excite and engage our girls to be creative and confident with technology in an ever-changing and increasingly connected world.
We equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and understanding to become responsible and digitally literate citizens, while developing their creativity, problem-solving and computational thinking.
Computer Science
Syllabus
Our Computer Science curriculum develops progressively from the Early Years onwards, with online safety embedded throughout. All girls sign an Internet Safety Agreement each academic year, with additional activities taking place around Safer Internet Day in February.
Coding begins in Reception with Bee-Bots, where girls learn the fundamentals of sequencing, giving instructions and creating simple algorithms. They then progress to block-based coding using ScratchJr and Scratch, developing their understanding of:
Alongside coding on screen, pupils use robotics to put their skills into practice, developing problem-solving, logical reasoning and debugging through hands-on challenges.
As girls move through the school, they are introduced to Python, giving them their first experience of text-based programming and building on the computational thinking skills developed in earlier years.
Pupils also develop a broad range of digital skills across the curriculum, including:
Together, these experiences help girls become confident and capable users of technology, with the skills to create as well as consume digital content.
Dance is an integral part of the weekly timetable at QCPS, giving pupils the opportunity to develop confidence and physical expression.
Through Dance, pupils explore movement, choreography and performance in an inclusive and supportive environment. Lessons encourage them to work both independently and collaboratively, developing an understanding of how movement can be used to communicate ideas and emotions.
Dance also provides an important creative dimension to the curriculum. Pupils are encouraged to take creative risks and develop their own ideas, while building confidence in performing and responding to the work of others.
Language is the key building block of culture and social interaction. At QCPS, we aim to ignite a love for English language and literature by promoting an exciting and effective curriculum, equipping our pupils with the essential language skills they need to communicate successfully and creatively.
We encourage a lifelong passion for reading in all the girls at QCPS and instil in them an ability to engage with, question and challenge any text that they encounter.

Syllabus
We have a creative, theme-based curriculum in Reception and Form I, where cross-curricular links are made at every opportunity.
From Form II to VI, the curriculum ensures the pupils access a variety of text types and have the opportunity to write in many different styles. From narrative to newspapers, discursive to descriptive, all pupils will master a range of skills within these genres.
Amongst many other skills, the girls will learn:
These skills will prepare them to be confident and competent readers, writers, speakers and listeners in years to come.
How to draw inferences
To predict; to summarise, discuss and evaluate
To reason and use evidence
To make ambitious choices of language
To proofread
To draft and edit
To write creatively and fluently
To engage a reader
Workshops & Educational Visits
The department seeks to employ a full range of learning styles, catering for all educational needs. Drama workshops which cross over into history, trips to the theatre, author visits and Public Speaking Week are just some of the many ways in which QCPS seeks to enrich the curriculum and inspire our pupils.
Geography at QCPS is an opportunity for our pupils to explore our planet.
Our lessons inspire a wonder of the natural environment such as:
Our aim is to ensure we support the girls to become confident collecting, analysing and interacting with a range of data gathered through their experiences. They also learn to use an atlas, follow directions and other basic mapping skills.
Geography
Mountains
Volcanoes
The effect of weather and climate
Workshops & Educational Visits
We take advantage of our local area and embrace the vast opportunities available on our doorstep. Geography field trip activities include trips to local farms, orienteering excursions, boat trips on the River Thames and a variety of excellent workshops and exhibitions provided by The Natural History Museum.
From cultural awareness to diving headfirst into new and exciting experiences, Geography can work wonders on the minds of young children. It’s a scholastic way to broaden their minds through complete immersion!
At QCPS, History is integral to our curriculum, providing context to our contemporary global topics. Our teaching approach generates an enthusiastic and enduring interest in the subject. It allows our pupils to develop skills of enquiry and analysis, helping them to think for themselves and arrive at logical and reasoned judgements.
History fires the curiosity of our pupils, helping to cultivate an interest of the past.
During lessons, the girls consider how the past, and its relevance to the present, impact on the world today.
Pre-Prep Syllabus
In the Pre-Prep, the pupils enjoy learning about how London has changed over time, studying topics from the Great Fire of London to Florence Nightingale.
Prep Syllabus
In the Prep department, the girls explore a range of cultural histories, such as:
We teach the girls to consider alternative viewpoints, encouraging them to consider how a range of people would have reacted and reflected on the events they experienced.
The Egyptians
First and Second World War
Workshops & Educational Visits
QCPS employs varied teaching techniques including traditional historical enquiry, role-play and visits to places of historical interest and discussion.
Educational visits by all classes take place regularly to a wide variety of historical buildings and sites, and of course, museums – The British Museum being a particularly popular destination. Classes also visit venues such as Shakespeare’s Globe, The Museum of London and the Tower of London, as well as travelling further afield to visit places such as Bletchley Park, Hampton Court and The Ragged School.
Languages at QCPS are taught throughout all year groups by specialist and native-speaking teachers.
Languages
Pre-Prep Syllabus
In the Early Years at QCPS, our languages teaching focuses on sounds and gradually evolves towards reading and writing. With time, the girls retain vocabulary and gain confidence in making their own statements. They enjoy being able to communicate purposefully. The first time they realise they are able to do so is always very exciting!
At this stage the girls’ learning focuses primarily on sounds through listening and singing.
Pupils understand and communicate ideas, facts and feelings in speech and writing, focused on familiar and routine matters, using their knowledge of phonology, grammatical structures and vocabulary. At this stage the girls’ learning focuses primarily on sounds through listening and singing.
Prep Syllabus
As pupils’ knowledge of grammar improves, so does their communication and autonomy. In the Prep, they are able to extend their conversations to write and talk about themselves, their home, family and their school life.
Pupils are also exposed to French culture through a residential visit to France in Form VI, workshops, films, stories, songs and rhymes.
Years 4, 5 and 6 have a recorded assessment at least four times a year.
Form 6 exchange letters with l’Ecole Catherine Dior in Normandy and have the opportunity to spend a fun day with the children they have been writing to during the residential trip.
At QCPS we aim to develop a sense of enjoyment, confidence and competence with numbers and measures through structured teaching and learning experiences.
We follow the renowned Mathematics scheme, ‘Maths, No Problem’. This approach to teaching ensures children develop a deep understanding of topics using concrete materials and a focus on making Mathematics practical. We are determined to foster and nurture a love of numbers.
At QCPS our Mathematics mantra is simply - Maths is fun! We are proud of our excellent attainment, but high achievement in Mathematics is about more than completing assessments and results. We are determined to foster and nurture a love of numbers, a high level of confidence in, and enjoyment of, Mathematics in all aspects of everyday life.
Mathematics
Advanced Learners and Additional Support
Stretching and challenging our girls is at the heart of our lessons and we always provide plenty of opportunity for differentiation. Advanced learners are now no longer accelerated through new content but are challenged with rich and sophisticated problems within the topic being studied, stretching their understanding even further. Those children who are not sufficiently fluent are provided with additional support to consolidate their understanding before moving on.
At QCPS we firmly believe that music enriches our lives and we strive, above all, to foster a love and appreciation for music in every pupil. As Plato said, “I would teach children music, physics and philosophy; but most importantly music, for the patterns in music and all the arts are the keys to learning.”
All pupils, from Reception to Form VI, receive specialist music teaching covering the main
A creative curriculum approach links music with other subjects, making learning more relevant, immersive and fun. We believe all girls should receive instrumental tuition; therefore, we include lessons on various instruments, from whole-class ocarina, recorder and ukulele lessons, to African drumming and Indonesian gamelan music.
Music
Listening
Appraising
Composing
Performing
Music Facilities
The music department includes five bespoke music-teaching rooms, a large music classroom and the Hall, with its handcrafted S4 Yamaha grand piano. Girls have access to a host of classroom percussion instruments, as well as class sets of ukuleles, djembe and dun-dun drums, marimbas, plus online music software to aid independent home learning.
Workshops & Concerts
Pupils perform regularly throughout the year, both at large whole-school events and at smaller, informal class concerts. We attend concerts around London and take part in various music workshops in and outside of school.
At QCPS, the girls lead healthy active lives, with a rich and varied physical education programme that gives everyone the chance to develop competence and confidence.
We offer a very broad range of individual and team sports, including both indoor and outdoor activities. The PE curriculum allows all abilities to succeed in sport.

Inspection Reports
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) is the body approved by the Department for Education for the purpose of inspecting schools belonging to the Independent Schools Council (ISC) Associations and reporting on compliance with independent school regulations. ISI inspections are also carried out under arrangements of the ISC Associations for the maintenance and improvement of the quality of their membership.
Highlights From our Recent ISI Report
Our most recent Focused Compliance and Educational Quality Inspection Report was carried out by ISI in February 2025. Here are some of the highlights from the Report:
“Leaders have created a positive environment where pupils enjoy their learning. Pupils flourish academically and personally because of the many opportunities made available to them. "
"The school successfully develops pupils' understanding of mutual trust and respect, within the school community and wider world. The emphasis on being kind permeates all aspects of school life."
"Pupils are highly supportive of each other. They are kind and recognise the value of service to others."
"Pupils are encouraged to be resilient learners, able to learn from their mistakes."
"Leaders have established a school community characterised by mutual respect and inclusivity. This positively impacts pupils' social development and fully embraces the school's values."
"Teachers' enthusiasm in subjects such as English, mathematics, physics and religious studies (RS) inspires pupils to learn, think for themselves and to achieve well."
Read the full 2025 ISI Report for Queen's College, London.

First for Girls
Since 1848
Queen's College, London has been changing the lives of girls since 1848. Founded to give young women access to the highest standards of education at a time when those opportunities simply did not exist, we were the first institution in Great Britain where girls could study for and gain academic qualifications.
Nearly two centuries later, our pioneering spirit remains unchanged. We continue to challenge convention, champion girls' ambitions and prepare young women to shape the future with confidence, compassion and purpose.
Experts in girls' education
Queen's has always been resolutely and proudly a school for girls. That commitment has never wavered because we know girls thrive in an environment designed specifically for them. In an all-girls' school, students are free to develop confidence, curiosity and ambition without the pressures of gender stereotypes or expectations. They are encouraged to lead, to question, to excel in every subject, and to discover their own voices. Our teachers are experts in educating girls at every stage of their development, understanding how they learn, grow and flourish both academically and personally.As pioneers of girls' education, we combine our rich heritage with the latest educational research to ensure every student is equipped not only to achieve outstanding results, but to become a resilient, compassionate and confident young woman, ready to shape the future.
A Proud History
Queen's occupies a unique place in British educational history. Founded by Professor Frederick Denison Maurice (pictured) in 1848, the College was created with a bold vision: to provide girls and young women with the serious academic education that had long been reserved for boys.
That vision changed the course of education. Queen's became the first institution in Great Britain where girls could gain recognised academic qualifications, and in 1853 became the first girls' school to receive a Royal Charter from Queen Victoria. From then onwards, the College's Patron has always been a queen, most recently Her Late Majesty Queen Elizabeth II.
Our pioneering tradition has continued ever since. Queen's has educated generations of remarkable women, including some of Britain's earliest female doctors, lawyers, teachers, diplomats and scientists, whose achievements helped open professions to women for the first time.
The opening of Queen's College Preparatory School in 2002 extended that tradition, inspiring girls from their earliest years and laying the foundations for lives of curiosity, confidence and achievement.
The Future Ready Curriculum
While our history is exceptional, our focus is firmly on the future.
The introduction of the Queen's Diploma in 2026 reflects our belief that education must prepare young people not only for examinations, but for life. Running throughout every stage of a pupil's journey, from the Preparatory School to Sixth Form, it develops the knowledge, character and practical skills that girls need to thrive in an increasingly complex and rapidly changing world.
Read more about our Future Ready vision.
175 Years of Pioneering
In 2023, Queen's celebrated its 175th anniversary - 175 years to the day since Frederick Denison Maurice founded the College.
As we look ahead, we remain true to the principles on which Queen's was established: that girls deserve an education of the highest intellectual ambition and that learning should continually evolve while remaining rooted in enduring values.
As Maurice himself wrote:
"We shall be glad to improve our practice every day, not alter our principle."
Nearly 180 years later, those words continue to define Queen's College, London.
Our Values
Prep values
College values
The Five Cs
At the heart of our the Prep School are our Five Core Values, known as the 5 Cs: Compassion, Curiosity, Creativity, Collaboration, and Courage. These values underpin every aspect of school life, creating a nurturing environment where children feel valued, inspired, and challenged to achieve their best. We encourage our pupils to ask thoughtful questions, think creatively, work collaboratively, embrace new challenges with confidence, and show kindness and respect to others.
By living these values every day, we help children develop not only academically but also as confident, caring, and responsible individuals, well prepared for the future.
Academically ambitious and pastorally led
We believe that outstanding education is about far more than examination success. It is about ensuring every girl feels known, valued and supported to become the very best version of herself.
We notice, nurture and champion the individual strengths of every pupil. As a result, Queen's girls leave us intellectually curious, emotionally grounded and socially responsible—equipped not only to succeed, but to make a positive difference in the world around them.

Leadership & Governance at Queen's
'The Council' is the name traditionally given to the Board of Governors that oversee both Queen's College, London and Queen's College Preparatory School.
The Council has responsibility for developing a vision for both schools and supervises their academic, developmental and financial strategies.
